claims: Issue #798 (opened 2026-10-24T19:03:14Z by amundsk, no comments when read) reports fourteen upper bounds at n = 334, 338, 343, 372, 376, 377, 379, 382, 412, 416, 457, 458, 502 and 504, each the exact rational side of s<N>_amund.cert rounded up at 12 places, from 18.786944251907 at 334 to 22.921326029542 at 504; it prints each certificate's exact side S' and the SHA-256 of each certificate and of its binary64 input, and calls each below Francisco Couzo's certificate at #763's source commit 964ee2b, the smallest public bound it found at the count.

The issue says every certificate is a dilation made with Evan Daniel's search/packer/dilate_cert.py (evand/square-packing at 7982d7a) on macOS arm64 with Python 3.14.6, from the binary64 packing beside it, with delta 1e-12, and that only each comment line was edited afterwards; it certifies the upper bounds only.

The author reports that Evan Daniel's two exact checkers at 7982d7a, verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), accept every certificate, with least wall clearances from 5.986e-13 (338) to 1.735e-12 (376) and least pair separations from 1.199e-12 to 2.340e-12, and that a third, unpublished exact check, a local workbench's rational certifier, accepted every float packing; the two public checkers share an author and the certificate format, which also made the certificates.

The issue says every packing was found from #763's certified packing at the same count: matched one to one by an optimal assignment on centres over the eight symmetries, 372 and 412 move no square beyond 0.1, so are refinements of it, and the other twelve move 1 to 29 squares beyond 0.1, so are new packings found from it. The searches perturbed 4,096 variants a round in a float32 GPU batch and polished the best 96 with Daniel's fq quench at n <= 400, and ran Daniel's explore.py for 15 to 30 minutes above 400.
The issue states no exact KKT solve and no rigidity or local-optimality analysis: only the upper bounds are claimed.
